title: Reservation Orchestrator: Intake API, Approval Lanes, and Capacity Planner
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Purpose: Design and deliver a Reservation Orchestrator that unifies how customers request reserved throughput, how those requests are triaged/approved, and how committed capacity is translated into fleet allocations and autoscale policies.

Background: Current dedicated onboarding is manual and inconsistent across sales, solutions, and infra. We need an intake API, a multi-lane approval flow (self-serve, concierge, legal-review), and an automated capacity planner that maps confirmed reservations to fleet allocations and autoscale configurations.

Goals: (1) Reduce manual provisioning handoffs by 60% for small-to-medium reservations. (2) Provide deterministic mapping from reservation SLOs (throughput/peak/TTS) to fleet slots and autoscale rules. (3) Surface key decision data (cost delta, risk, fallback model variants) to approvers and on-call.
acceptance_criteria: Customers can submit a reservation request via the new Intake API with required fields: estimated peak rps, 95th latency target, expected usage window, tenant id, business tier.
Requests are routed into approval lanes (Self-Serve, Concierge, Legal) based on policy rules and risk scoring.
Approvers can see automatic capacity recommendations (GPU slots, baseline concurrency, autoscale min/max) with cost and fallback plan.
Approved reservations trigger an idempotent provisioning job that updates the Dedicated fleet allocation and attaches an autoscale policy in the runtime.
Console shows reservation lifecycle, utilization forecasts, and an ability to adjust autoscale buffers while preserving SLA guarantees.
Audit logs record requester, approver, decisions, and the final provisioning events for compliance.
API and UI behave correctly in simulated load tests and integrate with billing and quota subsystems.
success_metrics: % of small reservations (<= 10k rps-hours) processed without manual ops intervention: target 60% by launch
Mean time from approved -> provisioned: target <= 15 minutes for self-serve lane
Reduction in provisioning incidents caused by mis-specified throughput: target -50%
Accuracy of capacity recommendations vs observed peak: target +/- 15%
proposed_flow: 1) Intake API POST /reservations -> validates payload, runs risk scorer, returns request id.
2) Policy router assigns lane: Self-Serve (low risk), Concierge (medium), Legal (high or regulated customers).
3) Capacity Planner computes recommended allocation: GPU type, reserved slots, baseline concurrency, autoscale min/max, buffer profile.
4) Approval UI surfaces recommendation with cost delta, fallback variants, and a one-click approve/decline. Approvers can request more info or run a simulated utilization forecast.
5) On approval, orchestration service enqueues an idempotent provisioning job that calls fleet-manager and runtime APIs to attach reservation and autoscale config. Billing entitlements are updated.
6) Post-provision checks run smoke tests (latency/throughput) and send success/failure to requestor and owner. Failures trigger auto-rollback and an ops task assigned to the provisioning oncall.
7) Reservation enters monitoring: utilization dashboards, forecasted exhaustion alerts, and suggested reconfigure prompts when usage deviates from forecast.
8) Decommit window supported: scheduled end date plus probation window with optional flexible extension via tenant portal.
capacity_mapping_notes: Capacity planner uses historical distribution priors (if available) and conservative headroom defaults. Mapping rules: throughput -> baseline concurrency -> GPU slot estimate -> autoscale range. Default headroom: +30% for 95th-latency SLOs; allow per-customer override in Concierge lane.
cost_model_notes: Estimate cost delta relative to current consumption and show monthly committed cost vs pay-as-you-go. Include quantization/variant discount options in recommendation.
rollout_notes: Phase 1 (internal alpha): enable Self-Serve for internal Redwood tenants and a small set of beta customers; measure accuracy and provisioning stability.
Phase 2 (beta): open Self-Serve to non-regulated startups; enable Concierge lane with manual review by Solutions Eng.
Phase 3 (general availability): add Legal lane automation for standard contracts, integrate with billing and reserved capacity commitment ledger.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-provisioning drives cost and churn. Mitigation: conservative defaults + post-provision autoscale tuning + cost transparency in approval UI.
Risk: Approval delays block customers. Mitigation: SLA-backed review windows per lane; auto-escalation to oncall after threshold.
Risk: Incorrect mapping leads to SLA misses. Mitigation: mandatory smoke tests with rollback and canary provisioning for large reservations.
dashboard_requirements: Reservation list with state (requested, approved, provisioning, active, probation, ended)
Per-reservation forecast vs actual utilization chart (hourly token throughput)
Autoscale policy inspector and free-form override with audit trail
Cost delta breakdown and committed vs used chart
